note: Triennial election of Lisnaskea Rural District Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. No contests. The Impartial Reporter of 22 May 1958, p. 7, records two changes — Mr. James Armstrong returned for Magheraveely in succession to Mr. John W. Irwin, and Mr. Thomas Maguire for Coolnamarrow in place of Mr. Denis Leonard — and notes that this was 'the first time for many years that Lisnaskea Council has been returned without an election'. Mr. Robert J. Liddle is returned unopposed for Derrylea (Reporter, 15 May 1958, p. 5). Other members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them, each division inferred from the 1955 return (Fermanagh Herald, 4 June 1955, p. 8). Filled from the Impartial Reporter's reports of Unionist selections (1, 8 and 15 May 1958): Ballindarragh, Corralongford, Maguiresbridge, Mullaghfad, Mullynagowan, Lisnaskea, Dresternan and Newtownbutler; each was returned unopposed (Impartial Reporter, 22 May 1958, p. 7). Dresternan and Newtownbutler were missing from the earlier record and are added. Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Aghakillymaude, Clonkeelan, Derrysteaton, Kulmore, Roslea and Springtown. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Armagh Manor, Belleisle, Castle Balfour, Colebrooke, Crum, Dresternan, Drummully, Eshnadarragh, Greenhill and Newtownbutler. Mr. J. Whittendale (U) was co-opted at the first meeting (Impartial Reporter, 19 June 1958, p. 4); a co-option, not an election result. division inferred from the 2 June 1955 return (Thomas Beagan); the Fermanagh Herald, 21 June 1958, p. 3 names the member as returned, sitting at the new council's first meeting. Printed 'T. Beggan'. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Checked on the Fermanagh Herald, 21 June 1958, p. 3 (w19-council-fix-west, Nov 2026): the meeting report prints 'Mr. T. Beggan' (kept in Name_As_Printed); recorded as T. Beagan, the spelling of his 1952 and 1955 returns for this division (the Herald's own nominations list of 4 June 1955 prints 'Roslea-Thomas Beagan'). Renamed from 'Roslea' to Rosslea (19 Nov 2026, w19-merges, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official DED name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Clones No. 2 Rural District) and the NI DED maps of 1921-39 name the DED Rosslea, as the rounds of 1924, 1930, 1933 and 1964 are filed. This round was filed as 'Roslea', the spelling of its source, kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (roslea) answers with a redirect to this one.
